title: AutoFence: Config change fencing, healing, and trigger synthesis for safe reverts
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Build 'AutoFence', a lightweight automated fencing layer that synthesizes safe rollback triggers for config changes, performs state-aware healing, and recommends batching/caching knobs when a rollback or staged remediation is executed. Goal: reduce mean-time-to-safe-recovery for config regressions while avoiding noisy or expensive false positives.
acceptance_criteria: AutoFence can ingest a config change event and produce a ranked list of rollback or remediation actions with confidence scores
When configured as an automated policy, AutoFence can pause a disruptive config apply (soft-fence) within 90s of detecting regression signals and execute a safe revert windowed by user policy
State reconciliation routine can restore KV-cache and prefix warmup sequences for at least two common regression scenarios without manual intervention
Telemetry: signal precision >= 85% and false-trigger rate < 2% on canary traffic simulated dataset
End-to-end integration tests covering canary fail, graceful pause, staged revert, and post-revert validation pass in CI
design_decisions: Use a modular 'fence + adjudicator + reconciler' architecture so policies can be swapped without touching runtime apply logic
Adjudicator uses a hybrid rule-based + lightweight ML scoring model; rules gate low-harm thresholds and ML ranks ambiguous cases
Soft-fence model: first 'pause / quarantine' stage where affected requests are routed to a shadow model/variant for up to 2 minutes before a final revert decision
KV and prefix warmup reconciliation will use incremental warmup + prioritized key replay (not full snapshot restore) to minimize cost
All automated actions must be reversible and emit a safety-ticket with links to the change, telemetry, and a one-click manual override in Console
implementation_plan: Week 1: Instrument change pipeline to emit canonical change events (author, diff, target routes, apply window)
Week 2: Implement Fence service to subscribe to change events and perform policy checks (rate, scope, risk tags)
Week 3: Build Adjudicator microservice with rule engine and placeholder ML scorer; integrate canary traffic signals (latency, error-rate, cost-per-token) as inputs
Week 4: Implement Reconciler for KV-cache prefix healing and a batched warmup path that replays top N prefixes
Week 5: End-to-end test harness with synthetic regressions and runbook automation; integrate Console UI hooks
Week 6: Pilot on internal runtime team traffic, iterate thresholds and telemetry, ship default safe policy
telemetry_kpis: Mean time from trigger signal to soft-fence < 90s
Automated revert precision >= 85% on labeled canary regressions
False positive rate for soft-fence < 2% over 7d
Average cost of healed warmup per revert < $5 (pilot target)
Number of manual interventions avoided per month (pilot target >= 4)
testing_notes: Create a small suite of synthetic regressions: kernel-scheduler mismatch, quantization-parameter drift, batching config error, KV prefix eviction regression
Simulate canary traffic with replay tool and assert fences trigger only when correlated signals (latency + error spike + cost change) exceed thresholds
Chaos test: simulate ZooKeeper/coordination lag during a staged revert and verify reconciler idempotency
End-to-end CI job that runs in PRs for Fence, Adjudicator, and Reconciler with mocked runtime metrics
